items.title: Morning Briefing: Nov. 28, 2026
items.excerpt: Here's a rundown of all the news you need to know for Saturday, including Türkiye, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia holding the second meeting of the Mecca alliance's Strategic Political and Defense Committee in Islamabad; hundreds of thousands of US customers are without power after a severe Thanksgiving storm; and UEFA opening disciplinary investigations into violence at the Besiktas-Hapoel Beer-Sheva and Marseille-Levski Sofia matches. Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said the primary goal of the Mecca Alliance for Joint Defense is to contribute to peace and stability by pooling member countries' military and defense industry capabilities, speaking after the second meeting of the Strategic Political and Defense Committee in Islamabad. He said decisions in principle had been taken on establishing a general secretariat as the civilian headquarters and a joint military command as the military headquarters, with most decisions approved and some deferred to the next meeting. Türkiye, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan reaffirmed their collective defense commitments and condemned Houthi attacks targeting civilians and civilian infrastructure in Saudi Arabia, according to a joint statement. - Hundreds of thousands remain without power in US as recovery continues after severe storm More than 400,000 customers were without electricity in the US, down from 656,377, with Pennsylvania reporting the highest outages at 99,317 from a storm, followed by New Jersey and Missouri, according to PowerOutage.us. FlightAware reported at least 2,489 flight delays and 144 cancellations within, into or out of the US as the storm disrupted holiday travel. Virginia Gov. Abigail Spanberger declared a state of emergency to support recovery efforts, following similar declarations in New Jersey and New York. - UEFA opens probes into violence at Besiktas-Hapoel, Marseille-Levski matches UEFA condemned serious incidents of violence and disorder during Europa League matches involving Besiktas and Hapoel Beer-Sheva in Georgia and Marseille and Levski Sofia in France, announcing disciplinary investigations into both. Clashes in Batumi erupted after Besiktas supporters displayed Palestinian flags during Thursday's match, with Georgian police intervening in the stands and the referee suspending play for around 30 minutes. Georgian authorities said officers broke up a fight among Besiktas fans, denying any link to the flag. Sixteen detained Besiktas supporters were released, and Türkiye summoned the Georgian ambassador. In Marseille, clashes between supporters left 11 Bulgarian fans injured, including five who were hospitalized.

items.title: US economy roars ahead in third quarter, inflation remains high in October By Reuters
items.excerpt: WASHINGTON, Nov 25 (Reuters) - The US economy grew much faster than initially estimated in the third quarter, while inflation increased further in October, reinforcing expectations that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates next month and again in early 2027. The sharp upward revision to gross domestic product last quarter, reported by the Commerce Department on Wednesday, marked the quickest economic growth pace in three years. It reflected upgrades to consumer spending and business investment, mostly related to artificial intelligence. Robust domestic demand is fueling inflation, with a measure of underlying price pressures in October posting its biggest year-over-year increase since late 2023. The economy has powered ahead despite the ongoing US-Israeli war with Iran.

items.excerpt: EMBARGOED UNTIL RELEASE AT 8:30 a.m. EST, Wednesday, November 25, 2026 # GDP (Second Estimate) and Corporate Profits, 3rd Quarter 2026 Real gross domestic product (GDP) increased at an annual rate of 4.3 percent in the third quarter of 2026 (July, August, and September), according to the second estimate released today by the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA). In the second quarter, real GDP increased 2.2 percent. The contributors to the increase in real GDP in the third quarter were increases in investment, consumer spending, and government spending that were partly offset by a decrease in exports. Imports, which are a subtraction in the calculation of GDP, increased. Real GDP was revised up 0.9 percentage point from the advance estimate, primarily reflecting upward revisions to investment and consumer spending. For more information, refer to the " Technical Notes" below. Compared to the second quarter, the acceleration in real GDP in the third quarter primarily reflected an acceleration in investment and an upturn in government spending that were partly offset by a downturn in exports. Imports increased more in the third quarter than in the second quarter. Real final sales to private domestic purchasers, the sum of consumer spending and gross private fixed investment, increased 5.8 percent in the third quarter, revised up 0.9 percentage point from the previous estimate. The price index for gross domestic purchases increased 2.7 percent in the third quarter, revised down 0.3 percentage point from the previous estimate. The personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index increased 2.1 percent, and the PCE price index, excluding food and energy increased 2.5 percent, both the same as previously estimated. Real gross domestic income (GDI) increased 4.4 percent in the third quarter, compared with an increase of 2.3 percent (revised) in the second quarter. items.title: Fed survey shows continued economic growth, sticky inflation in recent weeks By Reuters
items.excerpt: Nov 25 (Reuters) - Economic growth persisted at a "slight to moderate" pace across most of the US in recent weeks, while inflation remained sticky and employment levels rose, a Federal Reserve survey showed on Wednesday, two weeks before central bank policymakers decide whether to raise interest rates. "Prices increased moderately overall, as in the prior reporting period," the Fed said in its latest "Beige Book" report, a compendium of survey-based data and commentary from businesses compiled by its 12 regional banks to provide a read on economic conditions. "Contacts across a range of sectors reported sustained cost pressure from energy, transportation, health care, insurance, and tariff-related expenses." Still, input costs were outpacing selling price increases, suggesting growing pressure on corporate margins, the report said. "(C)ompetitive pressures and customer price sensitivity limited firms’ ability to fully pass through higher costs. Contacts expected both expenses and prices to continue rising in the coming months." ... The overall picture across the country was varied, with eight districts reporting growth and four reporting that activity was unchanged. Business investment — led by the artificial intelligence boom — remained strong, but consumer spending was flat as households were increasingly stretched and trading down.

items.title: ‘Daddy Cool’: Shah Rukh Khan grooves with Kareena Kapoor Khan in new song from ‘King’ - The Hindu
items.excerpt: Published - November 28, 2026 01:49 pm IST The Hindu Bureau ... ‘Daddy Cool’, the new song from Shah Rukh Khan’s upcoming action-thriller, *King*, was unveiled by the makers on Friday (November 27, 2026). Featuring Kareena Kapoor Khan, the dance number brings the two back on screen after *Ra.One* (2011). The song features lyrics and vocals from Boney M’s popular 1976 track while also featuring new Hindi lyrics that are written by Kumaar. ‘Daddy Cool’ is sung by Arijit Singh and Shilpa Rao and composed by Sachin-Jigar. The makers have also credited the original lyricist and composer, Frank Farian & George Reyam. The music video of the song features Shah Rukh and Kareena grooving to the beats in a retro styled, disco environment. Sharing the song, Shah Rukh wrote, “Back with Bebo... song Old School... but still Cool!” Earlier, another song, ‘Tu Mil Jaaye’ was unveiled, which featured Deepika Padukone and Shah Rukh. *King* is directed by Siddharth Anand and stars Suhana Khan, and Abhishek Bachchan in important roles while the extended cast features Jaideep Ahlawat, Arshad Warsi, Abhay Verma, and Saurabh Shukla, among others. The film is written by Siddharth, Sujoy Ghosh, Sagar Pandya, and Suresh Nair, and it has dialogues penned by Abbas Tyrewala. *King* marks Shah Rukh’s return after three years since *Dunki* came out in 2023. That year, the superstar also featured in *Pathaan*, also directed by Anand, and *Jawan*. The two turned out to be blockbusters at the box office. *King* will be released in theatres on December 24.

items.title: ILLIT's MOKA returns "step by step", BESTie's 'Love Options' tops QQ Music: November 28 news briefing — 노놀 매거진
items.excerpt: ### 1. ILLIT's MOKA: "step by step" On the 27th, ILLIT's MOKA thanked fans for waiting in a post on Weverse and asked them to wait a little longer while the members gradually return to activities. The agency BELIFT LAB said no specific comeback schedule has been set yet. Sources: Korea Times · Soompi · Topstar News ### 2. BESTie's 'Love Options' tops a QQ Music chart in China BESTie's 'Love Options', released in October 2013, reached No. 1 on QQ Music's 'Hot Songs' chart in China. In Korea it climbed as high as No. 5 on the Melon TOP100. It was also No. 1 on the Circle Chart's global K-pop chart for week 47 (the 15th to the 21st), announced on the 26th. Sources: Tenasia · Topstar News · News Culture (Circle Chart) ### 3. SUPER JUNIOR-D&E in Incheon in January, tickets for NCT WISH's added Gocheok show SUPER JUNIOR-D&E announced on its official account that it will hold the concert 'D&ESTIVAL: THE 15/15' in Incheon on January 9 and 10 and then take it to several Asian cities. Tickets for NCT WISH's added January 14 show at Gocheok Sky Dome open with a domestic presale on December 2, a global presale on the 3rd and general sales on the 4th, all at 8 p.m. KST. Sources: Soompi (D&E) · Topstar News (NCT WISH)
